p01.why: operator int and operator long both reach double with one conversion of equal rank, so no function is best and the conversion is ambiguous.

p02.why: A conversion function must not convert to a function type, and F is a function type.

p03.why: Converting 3 to D needs two converting constructors, int to A and A to D, and an implicit conversion uses at most one.

p04.why: The conversion of Source to double is ambiguous, but the ambiguous sequence counts as user-defined, so take(double) beats take(...) and the chosen call is then rejected.

p05.why: Contextual conversion can use an explicit conversion function only if its target type is bool, and this one converts to int.

p06.why: take(double, int) is chosen over take(Wrap, long) on the second argument, and its first argument has the ambiguous sequence through operator int or operator long.

p07.why: A conversion function must not be declared two times in its class.

p08.why: An array bound in new needs one conversion to an integral type, and S has two conversion functions to different integral types.

p09.why: A conversion function must not be static.

p10.why: Copy initialization is not a use that CVF-3 lists, so it must not use the explicit operator bool.

p11.why: Converting A to B needs the conversion function to int and then the converting constructor of B, which is two user-defined conversions.

p12.why: A conversion function must not have a return type before operator.

p13.why: CVF-1 says the target type can be auto, so by Tidal the program is valid and GCC 16 rejects it only under -pedantic-errors (Q-0059).

p14.why: Source::operator Target and Target(Source&) convert the lvalue s equally well, so the sequence to Target is ambiguous, take(Target) still beats take(...), and the chosen call is rejected.

p15.why: A conversion function must not have parameters.

p16.why: A switch condition needs one conversion to an integral type, and S has two conversion functions to different integral types.

p17.why: A return statement is not a use that CVF-3 lists, so it must not use the explicit operator bool.

p18.why: Copy initialization of x must not use the explicit operator int.

p19.why: A conversion function must not have ... as a parameter.

p20.why: An operand of a built-in operator is not a use that CVF-3 lists, so S{} + 1 must not use the explicit operator int.

p21.why: An operand of == is not a contextual conversion to bool, so it must not use the explicit operator bool.

p22.why: A::operator B and B(const A&) are equally good, so the conversion of A{} to B is ambiguous.

p23.why: A function argument is not a use that CVF-3 lists, so it must not use the explicit operator int.

p24.why: operator int is not const, so it cannot convert the const object s.
